items.stem: When do the monks eat their only meal of the day?
items.quote: The majority of the monks went out with their alms-dish, to collect food in town for their lunch, the only meal of the day.
items.why: The monks' day is ordered around a single meal they beg for.

items.stem: Early in the morning, who calls the novices together?
items.quote: Very early in the morning, a follower of Buddha, one of his oldest monks, went through the garden and called all those to him who had as novices taken their refuge in the teachings, to dress them up in the yellow robe and to instruct them in the first teachings and duties of their position.
items.why: New followers are led into their first duties by an elder monk.

items.stem: Where does Siddhartha place his hand as he speaks to Govinda?
items.quote: Siddhartha placed his hand on Govinda’s shoulder: “You failed to hear my good wish for you, O Govinda.
items.why: Siddhartha speaks to his friend with a gentle touch.

items.stem: After Govinda leaves with the novices, what does Siddhartha do?
items.quote: But Siddhartha walked through the grove, lost in thought.
items.why: Siddhartha is left alone with his thoughts in the grove.

items.stem: That night in the grove, the two friends sleep soundly.
items.quote: For a long time, the friends continued walking in the grove; for a long time, they lay there and found no sleep.
items.why: They walk and lie awake for a long time; neither can sleep.

items.stem: Siddhartha and Govinda follow the Buddha and watch him.
items.quote: And they followed him and observed him.
items.why: The friends follow the Buddha closely to observe him.

items.stem: Complete Siddhartha's words to Gotama: “Together with my friend, I had come from ____”
items.quote: Together with my friend, I had come from afar, to hear your teachings.
items.why: He tells Gotama the two friends travelled a long way to hear him.

items.stem: Complete: “Salvation from the ____ is what we Samanas search for”
items.quote: Salvation from the self is what we Samanas search for, O exalted one.
items.why: Siddhartha names the goal he and the Samanas seek.

items.why: Each person's action shows their part in the chapter.

items.why: The chapter moves from arrival, to the Buddha, to his sermon.

items.stem: When the friends reach the Jetavana at night, what fills the grove?
items.quote: And since they reached it at night, there were constant arrivals, shouts, and talk of those who sought shelter and got it.
items.why: So many seekers arrive that the grove is noisy far into the night.

items.stem: When Govinda wants to hear more from the woman, what does Siddhartha do?
items.quote: But Siddhartha urged him to walk on.
items.why: Siddhartha is eager to see the Buddha himself rather than hear about him.

items.stem: How does Siddhartha first respond to Govinda's eager question?
items.quote: For a long time, he looked into Govinda’s face.
items.why: He takes a long, silent look before he answers his friend.

items.stem: In the grove, what news about Govinda does Siddhartha give Gotama?
items.quote: And now my friend is going to stay with your people, he has taken his refuge with you.
items.why: Siddhartha tells Gotama plainly that his friend has chosen to stay.

items.stem: When Govinda speaks, Siddhartha seems to wake as if from sleep.
items.quote: Siddhartha awakened as if he had been asleep, when he heard Govinda’s words.
items.why: Govinda's words reach Siddhartha deep in his own thoughts.

items.stem: Siddhartha plans to leave Gotama without sharing his thoughts.
items.quote: Siddhartha continued, “but I do not want to leave the exalted one without having honestly told him my thoughts.
items.why: He insists on telling Gotama honestly what he thinks before he goes.

items.stem: Complete: “Don't forget, Govinda, that you are now one of the Samanas of the ____!”
items.quote: Siddhartha kindly spoke to him: “Don’t forget, Govinda, that you are now one of the Samanas of the Buddha!
items.why: Govinda now belongs to the Buddha's community.

items.stem: Match each place to what happens there.
items.why: Each place marks a stage of the friends' stay.

items.why: Siddhartha speaks with care, step by step.

items.stem: Put these events of the night and morning in order.
items.why: The friends' last night together ends at dawn.
evidence: For a long time, the friends continued walking in the grove; for a long time, they lay there and found no sleep.

items.stem: Why does Govinda begin, “it is not my place to scold you”?
items.quote: Right afterwards, when the Buddha had retired for the night, Govinda turned to Siddhartha and spoke eagerly: “Siddhartha, it is not my place to scold you.
items.why: Govinda wants to press his friend without giving offence.

items.stem: Why does Govinda press Siddhartha right after the sermon?
items.quote: But you, my honoured friend, don’t you also want to walk the path of salvation?
items.why: Govinda has chosen the Buddha and longs for his friend to choose with him.

items.stem: Even while objecting, what good does Siddhartha grant the teachings?
items.quote: The teachings of the enlightened Buddha contain much, it teaches many to live righteously, to avoid evil.
items.why: He gives the teachings full credit before naming his own need.

items.stem: That night, what does Govinda keep urging Siddhartha to explain?
items.quote: And over and over again, Govinda urged his friend, he should tell him why he would not want to seek refuge in Gotama’s teachings, what fault he would find in these teachings.
items.why: Govinda cannot understand why his friend will not take refuge.

items.stem: Siddhartha chooses not to argue whether living by the teachings brings suffering or joy.
items.quote: Whether it may be good or bad, whether living according to it would be suffering or joy, I do not wish to discuss
items.why: He sets that question aside to focus on one point.

items.stem: Govinda expects that Siddhartha will refuse the Buddha.
items.quote: Tell me, since it could not be any other way, that you also, my learned friend, will take your refuge with the exalted Buddha!”
items.why: Govinda takes it for granted his friend will join, which is why the refusal shocks him.

items.stem: Siddhartha answers Govinda “quietly, in a voice without ____”
items.quote: Then he spoke quietly, in a voice without mockery: “Govinda, my friend, now you have taken this step, now you have chosen this path.
items.why: He respects his friend's choice even though he will not share it.

items.stem: After the sermon ends, “many a ____ stepped forward and asked to be accepted”
items.quote: When the Buddha—night had already fallen—ended his speech, many a pilgrim stepped forward and asked to be accepted into the community, sought refuge in the teachings.
items.why: The sermon moves many listeners to join at once.

items.stem: Which words best show Siddhartha's care for Govinda as they part?
items.quote: Siddhartha placed his hand on Govinda’s shoulder: “You failed to hear my good wish for you, O Govinda.
items.why: Siddhartha's refusal comes with a blessing, not a rejection.

items.stem: Why does Siddhartha mention “the heart of every Brahmin” when praising the teachings?
items.quote: truly, the heart of every Brahmin has to beat stronger with love, once he has seen the world through your teachings
items.why: He measures the teachings by the learning he grew up with.

items.stem: The aside “night had already fallen” mainly stresses what?
items.quote: When the Buddha—night had already fallen—ended his speech, many a pilgrim stepped forward and asked to be accepted into the community, sought refuge in the teachings.
items.why: A short aside quietly shows the hold the sermon had on its listeners.

items.stem: “Their lunch, the only meal of the day” chiefly shows the monks' what?
items.quote: The majority of the monks went out with their alms-dish, to collect food in town for their lunch, the only meal of the day.
items.why: One meal a day reflects a life of chosen simplicity.

items.stem: Before objecting, Siddhartha says he hopes Gotama “would not be angry.” This chiefly signals what?
items.quote: “I wish that you, O exalted one, would not be angry with me,”
items.why: He objects as a respectful guest, not as a rival.

items.stem: Govinda's phrase “my honoured friend” shows he speaks to Siddhartha with resentment.
items.quote: But you, my honoured friend, don’t you also want to walk the path of salvation?
items.why: 'Honoured' shows respect: Govinda pleads; he does not accuse.

items.stem: In “This is what Gotama teaches, nothing else,” the Buddha sets firm, plain limits on his teaching.
items.quote: This is what Gotama teaches, nothing else.”
items.why: Gotama claims no more for his teaching than it offers.

items.stem: Siddhartha tells Gotama: “You have found salvation from ____.”
items.quote: You have found salvation from death.
items.why: Siddhartha's word is 'death': he names what Gotama has escaped, in his own terms.
